answer.body:
---
Touches: gateway/specs/endpoints/metrics.md, gateway/specs/endpoints/metrics.schema.json, gateway/tests/test_metrics.py, gateway/tests/_stream_rows.py, gateway/specs/endpoints/anthropic-messages.md, gateway/specs/endpoints/openai-chat.md, gateway/specs/use-cases/uc-1/, gateway/src/agent_gateway/
Origin: teststuffstash/homelab#3502
Class: build

---
## Deliverable

The four request-grain families — `gateway_requests_total`, `gateway_requests_incomplete_total`, `gateway_upstream_seconds`, `gateway_tokens_total` — carry a bounded `traffic` label (`real`, `synthetic`, `none`), so one PromQL selector returns real-traffic-only numbers.

## Why (the operator's text, 2026-11-16, verbatim)

The gateway's request-outcome series cannot tell synthetic traffic from real. `role` (prober, canary, worker, reviewer, …) is a label on `gateway_sessions_total` only; the request, response, upstream-latency and token families do not carry it, so a ratio over them mixes the prober's and the entry canary's calls with real rides. No KPI over the gateway's own traffic can be defined until that is separable.

**Wanted.** The request-grain families can be split into real and synthetic traffic with bounded cardinality (the metrics spec's label rules hold). Instrument only — no alert, no KPI in this change: it ships first so a baseline exists before anything is judged on it.

**Done when:** a PromQL query over the request families returns real-traffic-only numbers, and the metrics spec + schema state the label and its values.

Origin: operator, 2026-11-16 — "it needs to define and ship its own metrics and monitor + improve them"; the reference is oracle-fleet#1082, the first rollout here that declared the Prometheus metric it was going to improve. Ruled the same day: no Kargo for the gateway yet — the metrics come first, on the existing pin-PR deploy. Gateway island.

Live at intake (2026-11-16T21Z): `gateway_requests_total` carries `rail`, `dialect`, `status` and no role or traffic label. Seven days of dispatches: anthropic 653 (coordinator 238, reviewer 342, worker 66, responder 7), prober 40 (codex 20, openrouter 12, opencode 8). The entry canary rides as role `prober` (`canary.role` in the policy), so there is no separate canary role to read.

## Acceptance

1. `GW-METRICS`: each of the four families carries `traffic`, and the table under Spec changes is on `gateway/specs/endpoints/metrics.md`, proven by `gateway/tests/test_metrics.py`. `gateway_upstream_seconds` carries it on all three sample kinds (`_bucket`, `_sum`, `_count`): a `{traffic="real"}` selector over `_bucket` returns the same series set as over `_count`.
2. `metrics.schema.json` declares `traffic` once (`real`, `synthetic`, `none`) and lists it on the four families; no other family gains it.
3. Every existing exact series of the four families is rewritten with the label, in the same PR, wherever it is written. The value follows the session of the event that wrote the series — never one value for all:
   - `metrics.md`, the `series` cells of "Requests are counted by status", "Tokens and upstream time are observed per rail" and the incomplete-stream row of "Credential verdicts and transport facts": their events are worker and reviewer sessions → `traffic="real"`; the one `rail="none"` row → `traffic="none"`.
   - `anthropic-messages.md` and `openai-chat.md`: the `incomplete_total?` legends → `traffic="real"`; and the label-set sentence of `anthropic-messages.md` ("`gateway_requests_incomplete_total{rail,dialect,reason}` + 1") names `traffic` too.
   - `gateway/specs/use-cases/uc-1/`, per file: `opencode-response.json` (a worker ride) — its four series → `traffic="real"`; `openrouter-response.json` (a worker ride) — its one series → `traffic="real"`; `anthropic-response.json` — that leg is a `prober` session (its own `gateway_sessions_total{…role="prober"…}` line, and `anthropic-request.json`), so its `gateway_requests_total` and both `gateway_tokens_total` series → `traffic="synthetic"`; `release-response.json` — its `rail="none"` series → `traffic="none"`.
   - `gateway/tests/_stream_rows.py` → `traffic="real"` (its callers ride as reviewer).
4. No alert rule and no dashboard changes: `GoRailCredentialRejected` aggregates `gateway_requests_total` with `sum by (rail)` and keeps its meaning; its promtool fixture (`argocd/resources/agent-gateway/agent-gateway.promtool-test`, outside `Touches`) passes as it stands and is not edited.
5. `devbox run ci` is green in `gateway/` (the join and hygiene ratchets included).

Not checkable at the PR's head — the issue's own done-when, read after this change's pin PR syncs: `sum by (rail) (rate(gateway_requests_total{traffic="real"}[1h]))` returns data in Prometheus.

## Spec changes

Requirement: `GW-METRICS` on `gateway/specs/endpoints/metrics.md` — world `policy-default`.

Prose clause to add: the four request-grain families carry `traffic`, read from the session the request rides on — `synthetic` when that session was admitted with role `prober` (the role the probe ticks and the entry canary ride as), `real` for every other role, and `none` on a request no live session owns: exactly the answers whose `rail` is `none` — an expired or released token included, whatever role its session had (an expired `prober` token is `none`, not `synthetic`).

Family rows to edit (the `labels` cell gains `traffic`): `gateway_requests_total`, `gateway_tokens_total`, `gateway_requests_incomplete_total`, `gateway_upstream_seconds`.

New table, "Real and synthetic traffic are told apart". Legend (the page's shared one), plus: `one call on anthropic by a prober` = a `prober` session for stack `platform`, harness `claude`, then one `POST /anthropic/v1/messages` (the subscription rail is the prober's only rail in this world).

| description | world | event | series | value? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a reviewer's request is real traffic | `policy-default · upstream-ok` | `one call on anthropic` | `gateway_requests_total{rail="anthropic",dialect="anthropic",status="200",traffic="real"}` | `1` |
| a prober's request is synthetic traffic ⚖ | `policy-default · upstream-ok` | `one call on anthropic by a prober` | `gateway_requests_total{rail="anthropic",dialect="anthropic",status="200",traffic="synthetic"}` | `1` |
| a prober's tokens are synthetic | `policy-default · upstream-ok-cached` | `one call on anthropic by a prober` | `gateway_tokens_total{rail="anthropic",class="in",traffic="synthetic"}` | `12` |
| a prober's upstream time is synthetic | `policy-default · upstream-ok` | `one call on anthropic by a prober` | `gateway_upstream_seconds_count{rail="anthropic",traffic="synthetic"}` | `1` |

Two claims are not rows of this table, because rows already on the page make them and Acceptance 3 gives those rows the label. Both stay where they are, under "Requests are counted by status" — no second copy, no tombstone:

- "a served request is counted by status" (`one openai call on opencode`) → `gateway_requests_total{rail="opencode",dialect="openai",status="200",traffic="real"}`: a worker's request is real traffic.
- "a refused request is counted by its status" (`an expired token on /anthropic/v1/messages`) → `gateway_requests_total{rail="none",dialect="anthropic",status="401",traffic="none"}` ⚖: a request no live session owns has no traffic class; the prose clause above is what decides it.

One row to add to "Labels are bounded: sessions and requests" (the existing columns):

| description | world | event | family | label | values_within? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| traffic is real, synthetic or none | `policy-default · upstream-ok` | `every family driven` | `gateway_requests_total` | `traffic` | `real, synthetic, none` |

Sentences this change makes false: none found — the page's universal ("every label value is drawn from a bounded set declared in the schema") holds, `traffic` being a three-value enum.

Index row: none to delete — no `⚑ gap` names this.

⚖ pins (choices made, each with a plausible alternative):

- A three-value `traffic` label, not `role` itself on the four families. `role` (seven values) would also answer per-role questions and multiplies every series by seven, the latency histogram's buckets included; it is additive later.
- Synthetic is the fixed role `prober`, not a policy key: a key new to the policy loader needs the two-PR rollout (`gateway/README.md` §Test), and the canary's role is already `prober` in the deployed policy.
- `none`, not `real`, for a request with no live session: an error share over real traffic must not count unauthenticated noise.
- `gateway_provider_requests_total`, `gateway_provider_failovers_total` and `gateway_upstream_auth_rejected_total` do not gain the label (Out of scope).

Unverified — verify during implementation:

- The label's position in the sample line. The rows write it last; if the renderer orders labels otherwise, the rows take the renderer's order and the PR says so.
- That the `upstream-stream-truncated` world reaches the anthropic fake, for a synthetic row on `gateway_requests_incomplete_total` — no key row above asserts one; add it as a boundary row if the world allows.
- Read by the review at master `7f83fad`, in `src/` (which intake does not read): an expired token DOES resolve its session row, and the request is then counted `rail="none"`. So the session's role is in hand on that path and must not be used: `rail="none"` ⇒ `traffic="none"`. Confirm it, and add "an expired `prober` token is `none`" as a boundary row.

## Out of scope

- Any alert, KPI, recording rule or dashboard over the new label (#3503, #3504, #3505) — instrument only.
- `gateway_sessions_total`, which already carries `role`.
- The provider families and `gateway_upstream_auth_rejected_total`: the dead-key alert reads the latter per rail, and a canary ride IS a provider cell's evidence.
- `gateway_build_info` (#3501) — it touches the same metrics page and test file; the footprint hold serialises the two.
